concepts.label: fabric-attachment
concepts.gloss: A configuration binding on a leaf switch that attaches an access-facing port or endpoint to a specific fabric VLAN so its Layer-2 traffic is carried in that domain.
concepts.example: attach-leaf3-blue binds an access port on leaf-3 to tenant-blue's VLAN 1201, causing frames from that port to enter the VLAN 1201 Layer-2 domain.

concepts.label: fabric-vlan
concepts.gloss: A leaf-local IEEE 802.1Q Layer-2 broadcast domain identified by a VLAN ID and instantiated on a fabric leaf for tenant traffic.
concepts.example: vlan-1201 (tenant-blue) creates VLAN ID 1201 on leaf-3 as the local Layer-2 domain for tenant-blue.

concepts.label: leaf-switch
concepts.gloss: A top-of-rack or access-layer fabric switch that hosts endpoint attachments and local VLANs and connects upstream through the spine tier.
concepts.example: leaf-3 hosts tenant-blue's VLAN 1201 and its access-port binding while connecting into the fabric through spine-1 and spine-2.

concepts.label: fabric-mtu
concepts.gloss: The maximum Layer-2 frame size, in bytes, configured for a leaf switch's fabric or underlay forwarding interfaces.
concepts.example: MTU 9216 on leaf-3 permits fabric underlay interfaces on that leaf to carry frames up to 9,216 bytes.

concepts.label: svi-gateway
concepts.gloss: A switched virtual interface that provides Layer-3 default-gateway routing for hosts in a particular fabric VLAN.
concepts.example: svi-1201 assigns 10.20.1.1 as the Layer-3 gateway address for hosts attached to VLAN 1201.

concepts.label: spine-switch
concepts.gloss: A core-tier fabric switch that interconnects leaf switches and provides transit connectivity between them rather than directly hosting endpoint attachments.
concepts.example: spine-1 connects leaf-3 and leaf-4, allowing fabric traffic to transit between the two leaf switches.

concepts.label: availability-zone
concepts.gloss: An operational fault-isolation domain grouping or spanning a set of leaf switches whose availability is managed independently from leaves in other zones.
concepts.example: AZ-1 spans leaf-3 and other leaves assigned to the same fault domain, while AZ-2 represents a separately failing domain.

concepts.label: lattice-tag-3
concepts.gloss: An opaque, vendor-specific attribute stored on a leaf switch whose value has no model-defined semantics and must be interpreted by the Lattice implementation.
concepts.example: leaf-3 carries lattice-tag-3 with the raw value 0x9, which downstream Lattice software may interpret according to proprietary rules.
